---
title: "Cleaning your data: quality control"
---

Real genotype data is never perfect: some variants are poorly measured, some samples have too
much missing data, and a few errors always slip in. **Quality control (QC)** removes these
problems *before* any analysis, so that later results are trustworthy.

In this section you will apply a few standard filters, **one at a time**. After each one you
will look at a number in the log file to confirm it worked — so you always know you are on track.

::: {.callout-note title="How each step works"}
Every step has the same three parts:

1. **Why** — what the filter does, in plain words.
2. **Run this** — the command to copy into your terminal.
3. **✅ Check your work** — the exact line you should find in the log file.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Before you start"}
Make sure you have already [downloaded the data and tested PLINK](getting_started.qmd), and that
your terminal is inside your working folder (the one containing `pdac_gwas_demo_full.bed/.bim/.fam`).
:::

Every PLINK command writes a `.log` file (named after whatever you put in `--out`). That log is
where you check your work — it is plain text, and you can open it with `head`, `cat`, or any text
editor.

---

## Step 1 — Remove poorly genotyped variants {#sec-geno}

**Why.** Some variants failed to be measured in many individuals (a low "call rate"). A variant
missing in too many people is unreliable, so we drop it. The `--geno` filter removes variants
missing in more than a chosen fraction of samples (here, 2%).

**Run this:**

```bash
plink2 --bfile pdac_gwas_demo_full --geno 0.02 --make-bed --out qc_step1
```

::: {.callout-tip title="✅ Check your work" icon="false"}
Open `qc_step1.log` and look for this line:

```
--geno: 8480 variants removed due to missing genotype data.
```

If you see **8480** variants removed, you did it right — those are exactly the poorly genotyped
variants built into the demo data.
:::

---

## Step 2 — Remove poorly genotyped samples {#sec-mind}

**Why.** The same problem can affect *individuals*: some samples have too much missing data
across all their variants, which usually signals a low-quality sample. The `--mind` filter
removes individuals missing more than a chosen fraction of their genotypes.

**Run this** (note we now start from the cleaned file `qc_step1`):

```bash
plink2 --bfile qc_step1 --mind 0.02 --make-bed --out qc_step2
```

::: {.callout-tip title="✅ Check your work" icon="false"}
Open `qc_step2.log` and look for:

```
--mind: 25 samples removed due to missing genotype data.
```

**25** samples removed means success — those are the low-quality samples deliberately added to
the demo data.
:::

---

## Step 3 — Remove rare variants by minor allele frequency (MAF) {#sec-maf}

**Why.** Very rare variants (carried by only a handful of people) give unstable, unreliable
association results in a study of this size. We remove variants whose **minor allele frequency**
is below a threshold — here 1% (`--maf 0.01`).

**Run this:**

```bash
plink2 --bfile qc_step2 --maf 0.01 --make-bed --out qc_step3
```

::: {.callout-tip title="✅ Check your work" icon="false"}
Open `qc_step3.log` and look for a line like:

```
<NNN> variants removed due to allele frequency threshold(s)
  (--maf/--max-maf/--mac/--max-mac).
```

You should see roughly <span class="pmid">[NNN]</span> variants removed.
*(Exact number to be locked in from one real run — see note at the bottom.)*
:::

---

## Step 4 — Remove variants failing Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium {#sec-hwe}

**Why.** A strong departure from **Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium** (the expected balance of
genotypes in a population) often points to a genotyping error rather than real biology. We remove
variants whose departure is extreme (`--hwe` with a strict p-value cutoff).

**Run this:**

```bash
plink2 --bfile qc_step3 --hwe 1e-6 --make-bed --out qc_step4
```

::: {.callout-tip title="✅ Check your work" icon="false"}
Open `qc_step4.log` and look for:

```
--hwe: <NNN> variants removed due to Hardy-Weinberg exact test p-value threshold.
```

You should see about <span class="pmid">[NNN]</span> variants removed.
*(Exact number to be locked in from one real run.)*
:::

---

## Step 5 — Check that recorded sex matches the genetic data {#sec-sexcheck}

**Why.** A useful sanity check is whether each person's recorded sex matches the sex inferred
from their X chromosome. A mismatch usually means a sample mix-up. This check **reports**
problems rather than removing data automatically.

**Run this:**

```bash
plink --bfile qc_step4 --check-sex --out qc_sexcheck
```

::: {.callout-tip title="✅ Check your work" icon="false"}
Count the flagged samples in the result:

```bash
grep PROBLEM qc_sexcheck.sexcheck
```

You should find **4** samples flagged as `PROBLEM` — exactly the four sex discordances built into
the demo data. In a real study you would investigate and usually remove these.
:::

---

## Putting it together

Once you understand each filter, you can apply them in a single command:

```bash
plink2 --bfile pdac_gwas_demo_full \
       --geno 0.02 --mind 0.02 --maf 0.01 --hwe 1e-6 \
       --make-bed --out pdac_gwas_demo_qc
```

The result, `pdac_gwas_demo_qc`, is your cleaned dataset — the starting point for the next
sections.

::: {.callout-note title="Why we filter one step at a time first"}
Running the filters separately lets you *see* how many variants or samples each one removes —
which is how you catch a problem early. The order can slightly change the final counts, so for
reproducible results always report the exact commands and thresholds you used.
:::

---

::: {.callout-important title="A note on the exact numbers"}
The counts above for **call rate (8,480 variants), sample missingness (25 samples), and sex check
(4 samples)** are the artefacts deliberately built into the demo dataset, so they are the targets
to confirm. The **MAF** and **HWE** removal counts depend on the exact thresholds and on filter
order, so they are shown as placeholders. Run the pipeline once on the demo data and the precise
numbers will appear in the logs — drop them in here (or share the `.log`) and the check boxes can
state the exact figures.
:::
